error_chain: Kafka consumer poll() encounters a record with unexpected schema, KafkaConsumer throws SerializationException during deserialization
SerializationException is thrown before the record reaches Spring Kafka's MessageListener, so it occurs at the poll level in KafkaMessageListenerContainer
KafkaMessageListenerContainer catches the SerializationException in its ListenerConsumer.run() loop but it bypasses the configured ErrorHandler because no ConsumerRecord exists to pass to it
DeadLetterPublishingRecoverer requires a ConsumerRecord to publish to the DLT, but deserialization failure means no record was created
The correct fix is wrapping the deserializer with ErrorHandlingDeserializer which catches the exception and creates a ConsumerRecord with the error in headers
trigger_conditions: SerializationException occurs during Kafka consumer poll(), before records reach Spring Kafka's error handler chain
DefaultErrorHandler and DeadLetterPublishingRecoverer only handle exceptions from message processing, not from deserialization
ErrorHandlingDeserializer is the correct wrapper to convert deserialization errors into processable records with error headers

expected_answer.error_origin: Kafka consumer poll() deserialization in KafkaMessageListenerContainer before records reach the ErrorHandler
expected_answer.bypass_reason: DeadLetterPublishingRecoverer requires a ConsumerRecord which does not exist when deserialization itself fails
